Agra was a Mughal capital under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. This day trip by car from Delhi takes you to its two World Heritage Sites with an archaeologist: the Taj Mahal, read as a garden tomb and as a feat of planning and building, and Agra Fort, from Akbar's red sandstone walls to Shah Jahan's marble palaces. The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah or the Mehtab Bagh garden across the river can be added if time allows.

Transport from Delhi, the start time, meals and pace are arranged with you, and the quotation states exactly what is included.

What it covers

  • The Taj Mahal: the garden, the gateway, the tomb and the riverfront
  • How the Taj Mahal was planned and built, and what is still debated
  • Agra Fort: Akbar's red sandstone and Shah Jahan's marble palaces
  • The view of the Taj Mahal from the fort

How the time is spent

  1. Early start from Delhi

    By car on the Yamuna Expressway, with a briefing on the Mughal capitals on the way.

  2. The Taj Mahal 150 min

    The gateway, the garden, the tomb and the riverfront, read against the written sources and the building itself.

    You: mark the garden's plan and its axes

  3. Lunch 60 min

    At a restaurant in Agra, or a place of your choice.

  4. Agra Fort 120 min

    Akbar's red sandstone fort and the marble palaces added by Shah Jahan, ending with the view of the Taj Mahal from the fort.

    You: tell Akbar's buildings from Shah Jahan's

  5. Optional stop 45 min

    The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah or the Mehtab Bagh garden, if time and light allow.

  6. Return to Delhi

    Your questions on the drive back.

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Read the Taj Mahal as a planned garden tomb, not only a single building.
  • Distinguish the work of Akbar and of Shah Jahan at Agra Fort.
  • Separate what the sources say about the Taj Mahal from popular stories about it.

You take away

A plan of the Taj Mahal garden and Agra Fort, marked with what you saw.

Where
Agra, Uttar Pradesh
For
Schools, colleges, companies and the public
Length
A full day of about 12 hours, with 3 to 4 hours' drive each way
When
Any day except Friday, when the Taj Mahal is closed. October to March is the most comfortable season, and an early start means a quieter Taj Mahal.
Led by
An archaeologist or historian of Mughal architecture
Language
English, Hindi or both. Other languages on request, through our partners.
Group size
Agreed with you. Smaller and larger groups are welcome.
Starting point
Delhi, or wherever you are staying in the region.
What to bring
Comfortable shoes, water, a hat and sun protection. Much of the day is outdoors.
Travel
The car from Delhi and back is included in the price.
Meals
Not included. Lunch is at a restaurant in Agra or a place of your choice.
Entry fees
Monument entry fees are not included. The Taj Mahal's main tomb has its own ticket on top of the entry ticket.
Price
₹16,000 for 1 to 4 people, car and GST included
